note: All enumerations from the AI System Register Schema (Framework 06), sections on system_type, provenance, decision_role, lifecycle_status, human_oversight_model, and discovery_source. Values, labels and definitions are transcribed verbatim from the framework document. See ../README.md.

system_type.description: Traditional inventories were built for applications. AI estates contain three fundamentally different things, and the governance question differs for each.

application.label: GenAI assistant
application.definition: Conversational or generative tool used by staff

application.label: Embedded SaaS AI
application.definition: AI feature inside a product bought for another purpose
application.examples: CRM lead scoring, HR CV ranking

application.label: Predictive model
application.definition: Statistical or ML model producing a score, class or forecast
application.examples: Churn model, claims triage, credit scorecard

application.label: Rules engine
application.definition: Deterministic logic driving a consequential decision

application.label: Spreadsheet model
application.definition: Scoring or eligibility model in a spreadsheet

application.label: Browser extension
application.definition: AI running inside the browser session

infrastructure.label: Model API
infrastructure.definition: Externally hosted model accessed by API

infrastructure.label: Local model runtime
infrastructure.definition: Model running on local or self-hosted infrastructure

agentic.label: Agent
agentic.definition: System that plans and acts, invoking tools

agentic.label: MCP server
agentic.definition: Component exposing tools, data or actions to a model

system_type.rationale: Why the agentic category is separate. An assistant that drafts text and an agent that can write to a production database are not variants of the same thing, they are different governance problems. The inventory must capture what a system can do, not what it is built from. Local agentic components in particular, MCP servers on developer machines, local runtimes, agent frameworks, are the fastest-growing blind spot, and they appear in no traditional SaaS inventory.

provenance.description: Determines who you can ask questions of, and what assurance is available.

values.definition: Developed internally
Procured as an AI product
values.governance_implication: Contractual assurance rights should exist, check they do

values.definition: AI inside a product bought for something else
values.governance_implication: Never separately procured, so never reviewed. Highest miss rate.

values.definition: Consumer or free-tier tool used for work
values.governance_implication: No contract, no data guarantees, often no visibility

values.definition: Open model run on own infrastructure
values.governance_implication: Full control; full responsibility for evaluation

values.definition: Installed by an individual user

provenance.note: embedded_feature is the field that finds the most systems. The feature was switched on without a separate purchase, so it never reached a procurement gate, never got a security review, and never reached any register. Treat every embedded AI feature as in scope until ruled out.

decision_role.description: The single highest-value field in the register. It determines regulatory exposure, drives Framework 03's D4 and D5 dimensions, and is the field most disclosure obligations turn on. It is also the one most often recorded optimistically.

values.definition: The system decides. No person reviews before the outcome takes effect.
values.test: Does the outcome reach the person without a human seeing it?

values.definition: A person nominally reviews, but in practice defers
values.test: Is override technically available but rare, under throughput pressure, or without independent grounds to disagree?

values.definition: A person genuinely reviews and can overturn, with capacity and authority
values.test: Does the reviewer have time, information and standing to disagree, and do they measurably do so?

values.definition: One input among several; the person decides independently
values.test: Would the decision be made anyway, differently sourced?

values.definition: Produces no decision or action consequence

decision_role.note: The supports_determinative category is deliberate and is the most important design choice in the schema. Most registers offer only "makes" or "supports", and almost everything gets recorded as "supports" because a human is nominally in the loop. That collapses the distinction between real oversight and a rubber stamp, and rubber-stamped human-in-the-loop is the most common false control in AI governance.
decision_role.evidence_test: If you cannot state the override rate for a system recorded as supports_genuine, you do not know that it is. An override rate near zero means the classification is supports_determinative, whatever the process document says. Measure it before claiming it.

values.definition: Under consideration; not built
Being built
Pilot with real data or real users
values.register_implication: Full obligations apply. A pilot touching real people is not exempt.

values.definition: Live in production
Temporarily stopped
Decommissioning in progress
No longer in use
Assessed and excluded

rules: A register showing only live systems misses the one going to production next month.
Retired entries are never deleted, because "what were we using in March" is a question that gets asked after an incident.

values.definition: No human involvement in the loop
Human monitors and can intervene, but does not approve individually
A defined sample is reviewed after the fact
Human approves each consequential output before effect
System advises only; the human makes the decision

human_oversight_model.consistency_rule: This field must be coherent with decision_role and autonomy_level. A system recorded as in_the_loop oversight and makes decision role is internally contradictory, one of the two is wrong. The validator must flag this pairing.

discovery_source.description: Record how each entry was found. This field is the register's own quality metric. If 95% of entries are declared_by_team, discovery has not run. A healthy mature register shows most new entries arriving through intake_process, because the front door is working, and continues to show a trickle from technical layers, because it always will.
